cues.en: Welcome back to ScienceClick. Today, how to visualise general relativity. The goal of this video is to show different representations of the theory, and to put forward a brand new one, which I have not yet encountered, although it possesses a great number of qualities. The idea behind this new representation is to make the best possible use of the video format, and in particular its temporal dimension, in order to faithfully reproduce what the mathematics tell us.
cues.zh: 欢迎回到 ScienceClick。今天我们来聊聊如何将广义相对论可视化。本期视频旨在展示该理论的不同表现形式，并提出一种全新的视角；虽然这种视角我此前从未见过，但它却有着诸多优点。这一新表示法背后的核心思路，是最大化利用视频这种载体，特别是其时间维度，来忠实地还原数学语言所揭示的规律。

cues.en: In middle school and then high school, we learn that freefall can be modelled by a force. It's the force of gravity. This force allows us to predict the movement of objects, stating that they are attracted to each other, and in particular to massive objects like the earth. However, this description is merely an approximation, and it fails when the pull is too strong, such as the path of Mercury around the sun.
cues.zh: 在初中和高中时，我们学过自由落体可以建模为一种力。这就是万有引力。这种力让我们能够预测物体的运动，它表明物体之间会相互吸引，尤其是会被像地球这样的大质量物体吸引。然而，这种描述只是一种近似，在引力极强的情况下就会失效，比如水星绕太阳运行的轨道。

cues.en: It was in 1915 that Albert Einstein proposed a new theory, a rigorous mathematical model, which made it possible to describe freefall more accurately. For Einstein, there is no such thing as a force that would act at a distance. It is the fabric of the universe itself, which gets distorted and drags objects into a fall.
cues.zh: 直到 1915 年，Albert Einstein 提出了一个全新的理论，一个严谨的数学模型，使得更精确地描述自由落体成为可能。在 Einstein 看来，根本不存在所谓的超距作用力。而是宇宙织构本身发生了扭曲，从而牵引着物体坠落。

cues.en: In order to grasp this very complex theory, it is important to design visualisations that make it more intuitive. The representation that is most often used is that of a large elastic sheet, on which massive objects are placed. By deforming the fabric under their weight, the more massive objects pull everything in their direction, like marbles in a bowl. At first, this image seems to have two advantages.
cues.zh: 为了理解这一极为复杂的理论，设计出能让它更直观的可视化方案至关重要。最常被使用的图像是一张巨大的弹性薄膜，大质量物体放置其上。质量越大的物体因自身重量使薄膜变形，进而将周围的一切拉向自己，就像碗里的弹珠一样。乍一看，这种图像似乎有两个好处。

cues.en: It is very simple and intuitive, and it helps us understand that bodies attract each other indirectly, through an underlying fabric, space-time, whose geometry can be altered. However, although it is extremely widespread, this way of presenting general relativity has a large number of problems, which make it not very rigorous. In this video, we will try to improve this image by making four major changes. To begin with,
cues.zh: 它非常简单直观，有助于我们理解物体并非直接相吸，而是通过底层的时空织构间接吸引，且时空的几何形态是可以被改变的。然而，尽管这种表现广义相对论的方式流传极广，却存在诸多漏洞，显得并不严谨。在本期视频中，我们将尝试做出四处重大改动来完善这幅图像。首先，

cues.en: The image of the elastic sheet seems to indicate that objects are placed on space-time, like marbles, while in reality, space-time is the fabric of the universe that contains them. Therefore, one improvement that we can start with is to flatten objects onto the surface, so that it is clear that they are not exterior but contained within space-time. Next, one of the biggest problems with this representation is that it sort of explains gravity
cues.zh: 弹性薄膜的图像似乎表明物体是像弹珠一样放置在时空“之上”的，而现实中，时空是容纳它们的宇宙织构。因此，我们首先能做的一项改进，就是把物体压平到曲面上，从而明确它们并非独立于时空之外，而是被包含在时空之内。其次，这种表示法最大的问题之一在于，它在某种程度上是用引力

cues.en: by gravity. To the question, why does the apple fall on Earth, this visualization seems to answer that it is because the apple is pulled downwards, which causes it to fall like a marble in a bowl. But it is not acceptable to explain gravity inside space-time, using gravity outside space-time. We hence have to find a better explanation. In particular, it is more rigorous to say that if objects follow the well created by the Earth,
cues.zh: 来解释引力。面对“苹果为何落向地球”这一问题，这种可视化给出的答案似乎是：因为苹果被向下拉扯，导致它像碗里的弹珠一样滚落。但用时空之外的引力来解释时空之内的引力，是站不住脚的。因此我们必须找到更合理的解释。更严谨的说法是：物体之所以沿着地球压出的凹陷移动，

cues.en: It is because they move in a straight line, but within a curved geometry. When they fall, objects move straight ahead, but the curvature of spacetime gives us the impression that these trajectories are deflected. To understand, we can imagine the surface of a sphere, on which two ants would head north. At the start, the two paths are parallel, and we might think that as they progress straight ahead, the two trajectories will never cross.
cues.zh: 是因为它们沿着直线运动，只是身处于弯曲的几何空间中。在下落时，物体其实是一直沿直线前行的，但时空的弯曲让我们产生了轨迹发生偏转的错觉。为了便于理解，我们可以想象一个球体表面，两只蚂蚁正朝北行进。一开始，两条路线彼此平行，我们可能会认为只要它们一直笔直向前，两条轨迹就永远不会相交。

cues.en: However, the two ants end up meeting at the North Pole. This is possible thanks to the curved geometry of the sphere, on which straight lines tend to get closer to one another. Inside spacetime, the phenomenon is similar, and objects seem to attract each other when they are simply following the curved geometry in straight lines. However, this picture of an elastic sheet is still misleading. Indeed, one could think that if spacetime can bend,
cues.zh: 不过，这两只蚂蚁最终会在北极相遇。这得益于球面的弯曲几何：在球面上，直线往往会彼此靠近。在时空内部，现象也类似：物体看似相互吸引，其实只是在沿着弯曲几何走直线。不过，这张“弹性薄片”的图景仍然有误导性。的确，人们可能会以为，如果时空能够弯曲，

cues.en: it is due to the existence of a higher dimension. Here, for example, the two-dimensional sheet seems to bend into a third dimension. In reality, this is not the case, and the mathematics of relativity do not require any higher dimension for the universe to bend. It is therefore preferable not to represent this sheet seen from the side, but rather from the top, with a grid to illustrate the curvature.
cues.zh: 那是因为存在一个更高维度的空间。比如这里，二维薄片看起来像是弯进了第三维。但现实中并非如此，相对论的数学并不需要任何更高维度来让宇宙弯曲。因此，最好不要画从侧面看的薄片，而应从上方看，并用网格来表现曲率。

cues.en: While we're here, this also allows us to restore the three dimensions of space in which we live. Finally, the most important issue with this representation is the fact that our diagram completely ignores the time dimension. Spacetime is an object with four dimensions, three dimensions of space, but also one dimension of time, which can equally bend and curve. Faithfully rendering a four-dimensional geometry is strictly impossible.
cues.zh: 顺便说，这也让我们能恢复我们所生活的三维空间。最后，这种表示法最重要的问题是：我们的图完全忽略了时间维度。时空是四维对象：三个空间维度，外加一个时间维度，而时间同样可以弯曲。忠实渲染四维几何是绝对不可能的。

cues.en: and we therefore have to find a trick. A first idea would be to add small clocks to our diagram at each point of the grid. In this way, the space grid becomes a space-time grid and we understand that time can flow differently depending on where we are. That being said, adding clocks to our diagram doesn't give us much more intuition, and in particular we still don't really understand what causes objects to fall. If we drop an apple for example,
cues.zh: 所以我们必须找个技巧。第一个想法是在网格的每个点上给图加上小钟表。这样，空间网格就变成了时空网格，我们也能理解时间会因所在位置不同而以不同方式流逝。话虽如此，在图上加钟表并不能带来更多直觉，尤其是我们仍未真正理解物体为什么会下落。比如，如果我们让一个苹果落下，

cues.en: Why does it start to move towards the Earth? To really understand, it is necessary to remove one dimension of space to represent the dimension of time. In fact, it is the time component of the curvature, which explains gravity. With such a diagram, we see that the apple is always in motion. Even when it has no speed at the start of its fall, the apple is still moving in time. It progresses towards the future.
cues.zh: 它为什么会开始朝地球运动？要真正理解，就必须去掉一个空间维度，用来表示时间维度。事实上，正是曲率的时间分量解释了引力。用这样的图，我们看到苹果始终在运动。即使下落开始时速度为零，苹果仍在时间中运动。它在向未来前进。

cues.en: When no force is applied to the apple, the curvature of space-time will gradually bend its trajectory between a temporal speed towards the future and a spatial speed towards the ground. The apple moves in a straight line, but the curvature of space-time rotates the orientation of this straight line between time and space. We therefore understand that if the apple falls towards the ground, it is because it started with a speed through time.
cues.zh: 当没有力作用在苹果上时，时空曲率会逐渐弯折它的轨迹，使其在朝向未来的时间速度和朝向地面的空间速度之间变化。苹果沿直线运动，但时空曲率旋转了这条直线在时间与空间之间的方向。于是我们明白：苹果之所以朝地面落下，是因为它一开始就有一个穿过时间的速度。

cues.en: The curvature of space-time generated by the Earth has merely converted this temporal speed into a spatial speed. Having said that, as human beings, we do not perceive the temporal speed of objects. When an apple is dropped, it appears to us to be motionless. We do not perceive the fact that it has a motion through time. From our point of view, we experience the world instant after instant.
cues.zh: 地球产生的时空弯曲，仅仅是将这种时间维度的速度转化为了空间维度的速度。话虽如此，作为人类，我们无法感知物体在时间上的速度。当一个苹果落下时，在我们看来它是静止的。我们感知不到它正在时间中穿行。从我们的角度来看，我们是一瞬间接着一瞬间地体验这个世界的。

cues.en: And this diagram where objects form tubes over time, world lines, is not very intuitive. Our last step would therefore be to slice this diagram, to cut it up instant by instant, in order to form an animation which includes time. The curvature of the universe, which causes straight lines to dive into the earth, becomes a movement of contraction.
cues.zh: 而这个物体随时间形成管道（即世界线）的图表，并不太直观。因此，我们的最后一步是将这张图切片，一瞬间一瞬间地切开，从而制作出包含时间的动画。宇宙的弯曲让直线俯冲进地球，在这里就变成了一种收缩运动。

cues.en: The rate of this contraction is constant and perpetual because the curvature of space-time, which depends only on the mass of the Earth, is always the same. However, it is very important to understand that the geometry does not really contract. It's the fact that straight lines get closer together that gives this impression of contraction. The phenomenon is quite similar on the surface of a sphere. The curvature is constant on the sphere.
cues.zh: 这种收缩的速率是恒定且永久的，因为仅取决于地球质量的时空曲率始终保持不变。然而，理解几何结构并未真正收缩这一点非常重要。正是直线之间的相互靠近，造成了这种收缩的假象。这种现象在球体表面十分相似。球体上的曲率是恒定的，

cues.en: but the straight lines seem to be perpetually getting closer together. It is this representation, which I find to be the most appealing for visualising general relativity. The Earth, because it is very massive, deformed space-time, giving it a curvature. For us, the curvature of space-time appears as an endless contraction of the grid. In technical terms, we say that the volume contained between geodesics shrinks over time because of the curvature.
cues.zh: 但直线似乎总在不断靠近。我认为这种表现方式最适合用来直观理解广义相对论。地球由于质量巨大而扭曲了时空，赋予了它曲率。对我们来说，时空曲率表现为网格永无止境的收缩。用专业术语来说，由于曲率的存在，测地线之间所包含的体积会随时间缩小。

cues.en: This grid that shrinks represents what we call inertial frames, frames in freefall. With respect to this grid, a body that is not subject to any force will conserve its movement. Thus, if we drop the apple with no initial velocity, as no force acts upon it, it will remain motionless relative to the grid. But as the grid contracts, the apple will fall. With this image of relativity,
cues.zh: 这个收缩的网格代表了我们所说的惯性参考系，即自由落体参考系。相对于这个网格，不受任何外力的物体将保持其运动状态。因此，如果我们以零初速度释放苹果，由于没有任何力作用于它，它相对于网格将保持静止。但随着网格收缩，苹果就会下落。借助这种相对论的图像，

cues.en: It is also easy to see that the surface of the planet is constantly accelerating upwards, because it is always going against the natural movement of the grid. Finally, if we throw an object sideways with an initial velocity, no force is applied on it, and it will therefore continue in a straight line within the grid. But as the grid contracts, the object is constantly pulled back towards the Earth. That's exactly how the moon orbits the Earth. And the Earth
cues.zh: 也很容易看出行星表面一直在向上加速，因为它始终在阻抗网格的自然运动。最后，如果我们以一定初速度横向抛出一个物体，没有任何力作用于它，因此它将在网格内继续沿直线运动。但随着网格收缩，该物体会不断被拉向地球。这正是月球绕地球运行的方式。而地球

cues.en: orbits the Sun.
cues.zh: 也是这样绕太阳运行的。
